## Required Library
```r
install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)
```

## Syntax

```r
# Pipe style
df %>% select(col1, col2)

# Non-pipe style
select(df, col1, col2)
```
::: {.desc-item}
`df %>% select(col1, col2)` and `select(df, col1, col2)` keep only the columns you list.
The order you write the columns becomes the order of the result.

![](../assets/images/select_function.svg)
:::

```r
df %>% select(col_start:col_end)
```
::: {.desc-item}
Use `:` to select a continuous range of columns.
This is useful when the columns you want are next to each other in the data set.
:::

```r
df %>% select(-col_to_drop)
```
::: {.desc-item}
Use `-` in front of a column name when you want to remove it instead of keep it.

![](../assets/images/select_function2.svg)
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## When should you use `select()`?
Use `select()` when you want a smaller table with just the columns you need.
It is also useful when you want to move important columns to the front.
:::

## Examples

<div class="example-section">
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Keep only the tablet ID and weight</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

tablet_weights <- read_csv("data/tablet_weights.csv")

tablet_weights %>%
  select(tablet_id, weight_mg)
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Drop one column with <code>-</code></summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

tablet_weights <- read_csv("data/tablet_weights.csv")

tablet_weights %>%
  select(-batch)
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Select a range of adjacent columns with <code>:</code></summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

tablet_weights <- read_csv("data/tablet_weights.csv")

tablet_weights %>%
  select(tablet_id:weight_mg)
```
</div>
</details>

</div>

## Argument Overview
<p class="arg-intro">Required arguments must be included when using a function while optional arguments can be included on demand.</p>

::: {.arg-section}
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>.data</code> <span class="arg-types">data frame | tibble</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
The data frame to select columns from. In a pipe (`%>%`), this is passed automatically from the left-hand side.

```r
tablet_weights %>% select(tablet_id, weight_mg)
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> <code>data.frame</code> | <code>tibble</code></p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>...</code> — columns to keep or drop <span class="arg-types">column name(s) | helpers</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
One or more columns to keep in the output.
Use a minus sign to drop a column instead, for example `-batch`.

```r
select(tablet_weights, tablet_id, weight_mg)
select(tablet_weights, -batch)
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> column names or simple selection helpers such as <code>-batch</code></p>
</div>
</details>
:::
